sessions.label: AI Foundations Training · Session 1: Shift
sessions.cheat_sheet:
THE ONE IDEA
You direct. It makes. You write the brief (10%), AI does the making (80%), you check it (10%). The craft stays yours.

WHAT AI IS
A very well-read assistant that predicts the next word. Brilliant at drafts, options, summaries and structure. Trips up on facts, numbers and anything it can't see. Always check what it gives you.

THE FOUR BARRIERS, AND THE WAY PAST
"I'm not technical": you don't need to be. You talk to it in plain English.
"It changes too fast" and "too many tools": we use one tool, Claude, and go deep.
"I can't keep up": you don't need to. Keep using it and the hub keeps you current.

HABIT 1 · ASK YOUR CLAUDE, NOT ME
Stuck? Ask Claude first. Then #tpm_ai_training. Then Jem.

HABIT 2 · TALK, DON'T TYPE
Fluid Voice (free, Mac): fluidvoice.com
Open office: headphones with a mic, so it only hears you.

NOT SURE IF SOMETHING CAN GO IN?
Check the AI policy page. Still unsure, especially with client material: ask the leadership team or Jem before you paste it in.

THIS WEEK
1. Time · Money · Pain form, by Fri 6 Nov. The only thing you hand in.
2. Set up Claude page, about 40 minutes, before Tue 10 Nov.
3. Talk to Claude for 10 minutes about your job.
4. Post one thing it said that surprised you in #tpm_ai_training.
sessions.wrap_notes:
Good first one. Questions from the room:

Voice in an open office? Headphones with a mic. It stops the dictation picking up everyone around you.

What do I bring over from my personal AI accounts? Only live work you still need, using the Moving work prompts. Your client context comes in through the company Claude, not from old chats.

What about clients with strict confidentiality? Check before anything goes in. The leadership team is confirming the rules per client, and Session 2 opens with the AI policy, line by line.

Win already: one of the team had Claude build an After Effects set-up for a CCTV overlay. That's the shape of it: you know what you want, it does the making.

Next: Session 2 · Brief, Tue 10 Nov.

steps: New chat. Hold your Fluid Voice key.
Say the prompt below out loud, filling each bracket with your own answers. Rambling is fine. (Or copy it, paste it, and fill the brackets by voice.)

homework.prompt:
I'm setting up my personal instructions for Claude. Here's me:

Who I am: [your role, team and office, what you actually spend your week on, and how you think: creative, numbers or people]

How I want answers: [length, format and spelling. Answer first. One pick or options. Code blocks for anything I'll copy. Written for whoever's reading it]

What to push back on: [disagree with me, check the real-world cost, flag anything that risks time, money or a client, and give me a better option]

Honesty: [no made-up numbers, names or dates. Label estimates. Say when you're unsure. Check the AI policy before anything with client data]

Turn that into my personal instructions: a markdown file called instructions.md, under 200 words, talking to you in the second person, with a short heading for each part, in a code block so I can copy it.

Ask me a series of pertinent questions to understand more about my context and constraints before you get started.

big_idea.head: Bring it the problem, not your solution.
body: Most of us come to Claude with the answer already in our head. Write me three captions. Make this shorter. That's us doing the thinking and using Claude as a typist.
Describe the problem instead: what's going on, who it's for, what good looks like. Let it suggest the way through, then push back.
We've moved from the era of what can AI do to what do I need done.

framework.head: ICC: brief it like a person.
framework.intro: Every good brief, to a colleague or to Claude, has three parts.

split.d: The ask. What you want made, and what done looks like.
The background. Who it's for, what's happened, what you've tried, the files that matter.
The mandatories. Length, format, tone, deadline, and what it must not do.

framework.twist: The twist: talk it, don't type it. ICC out loud in Fluid Voice is a full brief in thirty seconds.

instructions.head: Set it once. It shows up in every chat.

items.d: Your role, team and office, what you actually spend your week on, and how you think: creative, numbers or people.
Length, format and spelling. Answer first. One pick or options. Code blocks for anything you'll copy. Write for whoever's reading it.
Tell it to disagree with you, check the real-world cost, flag anything that risks time, money or a client, and give you a better option.
No made-up numbers, names or dates. Estimates labelled as estimates. It says when it's unsure. Anything with client data checks the AI policy.

instructions.closer: Ask me a series of pertinent questions to understand more about my context and constraints before you get started.
instructions.note: Swap the creative director line for your own role and it works the same.

remember.d: It covers everything you'll do. Want more? Ask Jem before you switch up.
